title: Anchorage conduits move assets to a custodian without converting them, so the Token equals the asset supplied
content:
The three Anchorage instances are degenerate cases of the template. USAT's identifiers list `Asset Supplied By Spark Liquidity Layer`: USAT and `Token`: USAT (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.13.1.2.1.3/.4); USDT and USDC repeat the shape (.13.2.2.1.3/.4, .13.3.2.2.1.3/.4). Nothing is exchanged, wrapped or minted.

What the instances actually authorise is a transfer to a `Destination Address` — and it is the **same** address, `0x49506C3Aa028693458d6eE816b2EC28522946872`, in all three (.13.1.2.2.2, .13.2.2.2.2, .13.3.2.2.2). The limits are also identical: `maxAmount` 50,000,000 and `slope` 250,000,000 per day for each asset (.13.1.2.4.1, .13.2.2.4.1, .13.3.2.4.1).

This is custody, not allocation. Value leaves the ALM Proxy and becomes an off-chain claim on a custodian, with no receipt token and no on-chain position to monitor — the opposite end of the spectrum from the Aave instances, where the whole configuration exists to describe an on-chain position.

The shared destination is the notable risk feature. Three separately-documented instances converge on one address, so the per-asset limits do not decompose into independent exposures: everything sent under any of the three ends up in the same place, and the effective concentration is the sum. As with the shared Morpho curator and the shared savings implementation, the per-instance document structure presents as three risks what is operationally one.
description: USAT, USDT and USDC instances each list the same asset as both supplied and received, and all three send to one shared Destination Address with identical 50,000,000 / 250,000,000 per day limits.
